observations: BEP 44 defines an immutable item's storage/lookup key as SHA-1 of the item's flattened bencoded value v; get requests carry target=<SHA-1 hash of item> and a returned v is valid only when its SHA-1 hash matches target.

BEP 44 therefore does not expose an immutable put/get mode in which an arbitrary caller-selected 20-byte target is accepted independently of v; the target is obligatorily content-derived from bencoded v.

Git's traditional SHA-1 object id is SHA-1 over the Git object hash preimage consisting of type, length, a NUL byte, and the object's SHA-1 content; for a blob this is the familiar Git header concatenated with original content.

If BEP 44 v contains the Git object's bytes/content, BEP 44 hashes the bencoded serialization of v, while Git hashes its Git-specific object preimage. Those are different serialization domains, so BEP 44's immutable target is not generally the raw Git object id.
BEP 44 says storing nodes MAY reject values whose bencoded v exceeds 1000 bytes, adding a separate generic-coverage limit even if the key mismatch did not exist.
BEP 44 immutable items MAY expire after 2 hours without re-announcement. No passive lookup was issued and no independently pre-existing target residency was established in this slice.
probe.mapping: Both systems use SHA-1 content addressing, but the hash preimage is the binding mechanism. BEP 44 binds target to bencoded(v); Git binds object id to Git's object header-plus-content preimage. Equal hash width and algorithm are insufficient when the mandatory preimage transformations differ.
probe.assumption: The target must equal the existing raw Git SHA-1 object id exactly, with no external lookup table, chosen-prefix/collision construction, republishing, or alternate namespace mapping.
probe.rebuttal_or_discriminator: A viable rebuttal would require primary-spec evidence of a BEP 44 immutable lookup path that accepts an arbitrary caller-selected 20-byte target independently of SHA-1(bencode(v)), or a general identity proof that the required returned canonical Git bytes serialize to the same SHA-1 preimage under both schemes. The audited specification provides neither; it mandates SHA-1 of the bencoded item.
probe.inference: BEP 44's immutable-item mechanism is structurally incompatible with an exact raw Git-SHA-1 key bridge under the no-mapping requirement. It preserves a 160-bit SHA-1 target and supports response verification, but mandatory bencoding before target hashing changes the key derivation relative to Git's object-id preimage. This is a source-level elimination, not an end-to-end network observation.
probe.tested_scope: BEP 44 immutable-item primary specification and official Git SHA-1 object-name/preimage documentation only. No network GET/PUT, publication, hosted query/project, mapping service, protected authority, other-worker/downstream semantics, or target-residency test.
probe.scope_negative: Only BEP 44 immutable-item target/value semantics and Git SHA-1 object-hash semantics are in scope; no target-local filesystem/workspace coverage, no overlay-client implementation coverage beyond the specification, no mutable-item path, and no publication/residency evidence.

assumptions_uncertainty_residuals.uncertainty: A hash collision or specially constructed value could make two distinct preimages share a SHA-1, but relying on collision construction is outside the exact no-transformation passive-bridge requirement and is not a general object retrieval mechanism.
assumptions_uncertainty_residuals.residual: The immutable BEP 44 candidate is eliminated for exact raw Git-SHA-1 keying; separately, pre-existing residency and generic payload coverage remain unproven and need not be tested for this eliminated candidate.

frontier: BEP 44 immutable target is SHA-1 of flattened bencoded v, not an arbitrary caller-selected 20-byte key.
Git SHA-1 object id hashes a Git-specific type/length/NUL/content preimage, so equal SHA-1 width does not imply key identity across the two serialization domains.
The exact raw Git-SHA-1 immutable BEP 44 bridge is eliminated under the no-mapping/no-transformation requirement.
BEP 44 also has a conservative 1000-byte storage assumption and possible 2-hour expiry without re-announcement, but these are secondary after key-derivation failure.

Next bounded alternative is a role-local-deduplicated BEP 5 get_peers audit: test exact 20-byte info_hash key acceptance and whether any response path can expose canonical target bytes rather than only peer locations.
